newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX jumps to a new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX jumps to a new all-time high.

text.p: Keen domestic investors, eager to buy stocks on hopes that a rise which began last Friday would continue, drove the Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index to a new record high on Monday.

"Almost all stocks strengthened, and the main reason was probably that London markets were closed and supply was weak," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett. "It was a market of buyers apparently prepared to pay any price."
The BUX index finished at a new peak of 5,991.32 points, up 117.73 or two percent. The previous high of 5,985.17 points was reached on April 30.
"The Hungarian market, left without foreign investors, performed well and this means domestic investors possess substantial amounts to invest," another trader said.
But traders were convinced that as soon as U.K. and U.S. investors return to the market after holidays, high prices will enhance supply and encourage investors to profit-take.
"I expect a slight decline on Tuesday as I think many investors will mull selling their papers at these prices," Keresztesi said.
"The market will lose momentum when London reopens on Tuesday as there will be again arbitrage opportunities between Budapest and London," the other trader said.
Market participants said the current run on the Czech crown might cause temporary uncertainty on the Hungarian market but in the longer term Hungary was likely to benefit.
"Even if this causes some uncertainty, things will go back to normal as investors' confidence is strong towards Hungary," Keresztesi said.
The European credit rating agency IBCA on Friday announced that it had placed Hungary's long-term foreign currency rating on Rating Watch with positive implications.
On Monday, pharmaceuticals stocks strongly benefited from investors' eagerness to buy.
Egis Rt and Richter each gained 400 forints to finish at 11,600 and 14,900 forints, respectively, while Human put on 50 forints to finish at 2,700.
"Richter is still probably benefiting from the fact that it had such a (high) issue price and that it was oversubscribed," Keresztesi said.
In the second phase of its selloff Richter shares were priced at $78 and 14,160 forints and a package of 2.6 million stocks placed privately was four and a half times oversubscribed.
The domestic offer of 200,000 shares will start on Tuesday.
In a fresh development, Polish financial daily Rzeczpospolita said on Saturday that Richter was among several foreign companies which were to take part in the privatisation of Poland's Polfa Krakow.
Elsewhere on the market, chemicals TVK gained 35 forints to finish at 2,750.

Market participants said TVK was rising as investors who had sold TVK shares to buy oil company MOL Rt in its recently completed successful selloff phase are now reinvesting in TVK as heavy domestic demand for MOL gave them only a few MOL shares in the allocation.
